ActionApproval.description: One server-authenticated identity approving one plan revision once.
ActionApproval.title: ActionApproval

ActionCanaryStep.description:
One durably recorded widening of a canaried effect.

A canary walks a dial upward - 5%, then 10%, then all of it - looking at the
protected signals between steps. Each share is a genuinely different state
of the world with its own idempotency key, so each one is recorded here as
it lands rather than being reconstructed afterwards from the share that
happened to be reached last. That is the whole point: a worker that died
between two steps must leave behind the exact set of effects that are
standing, because a revert has to unwind every one of them.
ActionCanaryStep.title: ActionCanaryStep

ActionControlIntent.description: The complete mutation vocabulary exposed to a client.
ActionControlIntent.title: ActionControlIntent

ActionControlRequest.description: An operator's intent against one stable, server-held plan revision.
ActionControlRequest.title: ActionControlRequest

ActionControlResponse.description: Typed API response for the latest authoritative plan revision.
ActionControlResponse.title: ActionControlResponse

ActionControlSnapshot.description: Authoritative durable control state returned after every mutation.
ActionControlSnapshot.title: ActionControlSnapshot

ActionControlState.description: Durable progress of one immutable plan revision.
ActionControlState.title: ActionControlState

ActionGateResult.description: One measured deterministic guard result for the exact plan.
ActionGateResult.title: ActionGateResult

ActionGateStatus.description: Whether one deterministic safety gate admitted the exact plan.
ActionGateStatus.title: ActionGateStatus

ActionKind.description:
The rungs of the remediation ladder, cheapest and safest first.

The ordering of the rungs into ladders, and which rung a given diagnosis
earns, is operator-owned configuration - this enum is only the vocabulary
those ladders are written in.
ActionKind.title: ActionKind

ActionOutcome.description:
What one actuator call actually did, recorded whether it worked or not.

``dry_run`` and ``SIMULATED`` are the same fact stated twice, and the
contract keeps them in agreement: this is the single place that makes "we
were only pretending" impossible to confuse with "we changed production".

``deduplicated`` marks an outcome that was returned *without* calling the
actuator, because the effect this key names was already in place. It is not
a failure and not a no-op error - it is the idempotency key doing its job.
ActionOutcome.title: ActionOutcome

ActionPlan.description:
One concrete, reversible effect an actuator proposes to put in place.

A plan is built from a decision that already decided to act, and it carries
the safety-critical facts forward unchanged: the target service is the
origin the causal collapse computed from evidence, and the approval
requirement is the policy gate's, never the adapter's opinion.

``expected_effect`` is required because an action nobody can check is not
something this platform takes: it states, in advance, what ``verify`` should
find once the effect is in place.
ActionPlan.title: ActionPlan

ActionRollbackVerification.description: Delayed, read-only proof of protected-service recovery after rollback.
ActionRollbackVerification.title: ActionRollbackVerification

ActionRungSnapshot.description: The exact committed ladder choice from which the plan was built.
ActionRungSnapshot.title: ActionRungSnapshot

ActionSloSample.description: One immutable SLO reading with the exact targets used to judge it.
ActionSloSample.title: ActionSloSample

ActionSloSampleStatus.description: Whether both signals needed for one SLO judgement were observable.
ActionSloSampleStatus.title: ActionSloSampleStatus

ActionStatus.description:
How far one action got, and whether the world was touched.

``SIMULATED`` means nothing was touched - either the caller asked for a
simulation or the executor is in dry-run mode. ``APPLIED`` means the effect
was put in place; ``VERIFIED`` means it was afterwards observed to actually
be in place, which is a different and stronger claim. ``FAILED`` is the
honest answer when an actuator could not finish, and it deliberately does
not assert whether the world changed - only a ``verify`` can settle that.
ActionStatus.title: ActionStatus

ActuatorKind.description:
Which system an action is carried out against.

``SIMULATED`` is a first-class member rather than a test fixture: the
platform must be demonstrable end to end with no cluster attached, and an
adapter that touches nothing has to say so in the audit trail like any
other.
ActuatorKind.title: ActuatorKind

AgentAssessment.description:
One agent's evidence-backed verdict about one axis at one event time.

A calm axis (``SCORED`` at ``0.0`` with no evidence) is a genuine finding:
the claimed detectors ran and saw nothing. An axis whose detectors produced
no coverage is ``INSUFFICIENT`` instead, so absence of evidence is never
silently reported as evidence of absence.
AgentAssessment.title: AgentAssessment

AgentStatus.description: Whether an agent had the coverage to score its axis at all.
AgentStatus.title: AgentStatus

AgentTrend.description: Direction of an axis score against the agent's previous assessment.
AgentTrend.title: AgentTrend

AppliedSuppression.description:
The operator-owned window that held a decision back, and who owns it.

A window that could not name an owner, a reason and an expiry would be an
anonymous, permanent silence. All three are required, so every suppressed
decision records the person who took responsibility for it and the moment
that responsibility runs out.
AppliedSuppression.title: AppliedSuppression

AuditEntry.description: One immutable record, bound to the entry before it by its own hash.
AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry

AuditEventKind.description:
What kind of thing the ledger is recording.

Deliberately small. The ledger records what the platform *decided* and what
it *did about it*, which is the pair a person needs to reconstruct an
incident; telemetry lives in the stores that are built for it.
AuditEventKind.title: AuditEventKind

CausalGraph.description:
One durable graph revision for an incident.

Resolved revisions remain valid durable state so closing an incident can
advance both records atomically. The repository's current-graph query
filters them out.
CausalGraph.title: CausalGraph

CausalGraphEdge.description:
One topology edge rendered in possible propagation direction.

Configuration says ``caller depends on dependency``. This public edge is
deliberately reversed to ``dependency -> caller`` so its arrow answers the
incident-response question: where could an observed effect propagate?
CausalGraphEdge.title: CausalGraphEdge

CausalGraphNode.description: One committed topology service with evidence-derived incident heat.
CausalGraphNode.title: CausalGraphNode

CausalGraphResponse.description: The authoritative current-incident graph or an explicit absence.
CausalGraphResponse.title: CausalGraphResponse

ChangeEvent.description:
One recorded operator change, the raw material of deploy-correlated pressure.

A change is a fact about the system's own history, never a conclusion about
an incident. It carries its own honesty label because the MVP feed mixes an
operator-maintained ledger with changes observed from the cluster.
ChangeEvent.title: ChangeEvent

ChangeKind.description: How the system was changed by its operators, not by its callers.
ChangeKind.title: ChangeKind

CheckOutcome.description: How one deterministic check answered, including an honest vacuous pass.
CheckOutcome.title: CheckOutcome

ContextWindow.description: A trusted external event and the signals whose volume it may explain.
ContextWindow.title: ContextWindow

Decision.description:
What the platform decided to do about one incident, and what it may not do.

The decision is taken on the incident's strongest evidence rather than on
whatever the latest tick happened to read - a storm that has gone quiet for
a moment is still the storm - and ``evidence_ts`` records the tick that
evidence was measured at, so a decision never quietly presents old evidence
as current.

Three safety properties are enforced here rather than left to the gate,
because the contract is the last thing between a hypothesis and production:
an acting decision must be confirmed, must carry a verdict, and must name a
``target_service`` that was computed from evidence. ``requires_human_approval``
is derived from ``approval_reasons`` so a decision can never claim to be
approved-free while listing the reasons it is not.

**``approval_reasons`` and ``escalation_reasons`` are different facts and are
deliberately separate fields.** ``approval_reasons`` is *why a person must
sign before this happens*; ``escalation_reasons`` is *why a person is being
brought in*. They were one field until 2026-07-25, and the consequence was
found by running the remediation loop over a recorded capture: every
``AUTO_CONTAIN_THEN_ESCALATE`` decision - the platform's designed answer to a
verified attack, whose whole point is to contain the harm *and then* fetch
somebody - was refused by the executor for want of a signature, because
"a person is being told" had been recorded in the field the action plane
reads as "a person must consent". 98 out of 98 on `combo_night`. Containing
an attack and asking permission to contain it are not the same decision, and
a system that cannot say which one it means will always pick the wrong one.
Decision.title: Decision

DecisionAction.description:
What the platform does about one incident, on a graded ladder.

``SUPPRESS`` is silence with a stated reason - nothing is happening, or an
operator has taken responsibility for the noise. ``ALERT`` tells a person
without paging them. ``ACT`` is autonomous, reversible remediation.
``ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN`` hands the problem over untouched.
``AUTO_CONTAIN_THEN_ESCALATE`` does both: contain the immediate harm, then
bring in a person, which is the only sane answer to a verified attack.
DecisionAction.title: DecisionAction

DecompFrame.description: Full-resolution split of observed telemetry into explained and residual parts.
DecompFrame.title: DecompFrame

EpisodeStatus.description: Lifecycle state of an anti-flapping symptom episode.
EpisodeStatus.title: EpisodeStatus

EvidenceAxis.description:
The independent axes a surge is judged on, one agent per axis.

Each axis is scored from its own claimed evidence only. An attacker who
keeps one axis calm cannot thereby quiet another, because no agent ever
reads another agent's score.
EvidenceAxis.title: EvidenceAxis

EvidenceDirection.description: Which way a measured value sits relative to its stated baseline.
EvidenceDirection.title: EvidenceDirection

EvidenceItem.description:
One measured value that justifies part of an axis score.

An agent never reports a bare number: every point of score is traceable to
an item naming the feature, what was measured, what it is compared with,
which way it moved and how much of the score it contributed.
EvidenceItem.title: EvidenceItem

Incident.description:
One real-world problem, assembled from the storm of symptoms it caused.

A single fault lights many detectors across many services. An incident is
the collapse of that storm into the one thing an on-call person is actually
dealing with: co-occurring episodes on services that are near each other in
the topology become one incident, not twelve alerts.

Identity is anchored to the earliest episode in the cluster, so the incident
keeps its id as the storm grows around it.

``services`` are the services that carried a symptom. ``implicated_services``
are the ones named only by the evidence - a service whose caller's degraded
dependency edge accuses it while it emits nothing of its own. The two are
kept apart because they are different claims: one was observed misbehaving,
the other was merely blamed, and a real cascade's origin is routinely the
second kind.
Incident.title: Incident

IncidentActionLog.description: The decision plus every attached immutable action/audit record.
IncidentActionLog.title: IncidentActionLog

IncidentActionState.description: What was decided, separately from what an actuator proved it did.
IncidentActionState.title: IncidentActionState

IncidentConfidence.description: A calibrated confidence or an explicit refusal to display one.
IncidentConfidence.title: IncidentConfidence

IncidentConfidenceStatus.description: Whether the displayed confidence has a calibration basis.
IncidentConfidenceStatus.title: IncidentConfidenceStatus

IncidentDecomposition.description: The primary full-resolution incident series, or explicit insufficiency.
IncidentDecomposition.title: IncidentDecomposition

IncidentDetail.description: One evidence-complete incident revision for the proof screen.
IncidentDetail.title: IncidentDetail

IncidentDetailResponse.description: Ready/not-found/degraded response for one stable incident id.
IncidentDetailResponse.title: IncidentDetailResponse

IncidentEvidenceProof.description: One typed, independently scored evidence item behind the verdict.
IncidentEvidenceProof.title: IncidentEvidenceProof

IncidentEvidenceValue.description: One measured value compact enough for an incident card.
IncidentEvidenceValue.title: IncidentEvidenceValue

IncidentFeedItem.description: One evidence-first card in the authoritative incident snapshot.
IncidentFeedItem.title: IncidentFeedItem

IncidentProvenance.description: What was measured and how the stimulus reached the platform.
IncidentProvenance.title: IncidentProvenance

IncidentSeverity.description: How much this incident matters, in the language a responder pages on.
IncidentSeverity.title: IncidentSeverity

IncidentState.description: Where an incident is in its life, from first symptom to resolved.
IncidentState.title: IncidentState

IncidentVerdictProof.description: The winning class and complete support distribution, with honest calibration.
IncidentVerdictProof.title: IncidentVerdictProof

KpiKey.description: The four reliability questions on the command centre.
KpiKey.title: KpiKey

KpiMetric.description: One reliability KPI with enough provenance to interpret it.
KpiMetric.title: KpiMetric

KpiResponse.description: The command centre's one typed reliability snapshot.
KpiResponse.title: KpiResponse

KpiStatus.description: Whether a number was actually measured.
KpiStatus.title: KpiStatus

KpiWindow.description: The evidence interval behind a KPI, or why no interval exists.
KpiWindow.title: KpiWindow

Observation.description: One event-time telemetry value, containing evidence but never answer-key data.
Observation.title: Observation

ObservationFreshness.description:
How recently the platform last judged live telemetry.

Staleness is a property of the observation, not of any incident. An
incident card can only ever be the last thing that was measured; whether
that is *current* depends on whether anything has been measured since, and
a feed that cannot say so invites a stopped platform to read as a calm one.
ObservationFreshness.title: ObservationFreshness

ObservationStatus.description: Whether the platform is currently able to see anything at all.
ObservationStatus.title: ObservationStatus

ReasonSubtype.description:
A refinement that changes what a sane response looks like.

``CAPACITY_SHORTAGE`` exists so under-provisioning is answered with
"scale", never with "block": the traffic is real and the system is simply
too small for it.
ReasonSubtype.title: ReasonSubtype

RejectedAlternative.description: One diagnosis that was considered and the evidence that ruled it out.
RejectedAlternative.title: RejectedAlternative

RollbackVerificationStatus.description: What delayed protected-service telemetry can support after a revert.
RollbackVerificationStatus.title: RollbackVerificationStatus

ScoreHeadline.description: One compact metric from a score-proof artifact.
ScoreHeadline.title: ScoreHeadline

ScoreProof.description: Immutable output of one held-out scoring invocation.
ScoreProof.title: ScoreProof

SecurityCohort.description: One suspect cohort explicitly named by public telemetry evidence.
SecurityCohort.title: SecurityCohort

SecurityFeature.description: The security-view signals, whether measured or explicitly unavailable.
SecurityFeature.title: SecurityFeature

SecurityMeasurement.description: One scoped security measurement with evidence-window provenance.
SecurityMeasurement.title: SecurityMeasurement

SecurityMeasurementStatus.description: Whether telemetry supports a numeric security claim.
SecurityMeasurementStatus.title: SecurityMeasurementStatus

SecurityMeasurementUnit.description: What a measured numeric security value actually represents.
SecurityMeasurementUnit.title: SecurityMeasurementUnit

SecurityMitigation.description: Latest server-held surgical action plus independent cohort integrity.
SecurityMitigation.title: SecurityMitigation

SecurityResponse.description: The latest unresolved security snapshot or an explicit absence.
SecurityResponse.title: SecurityResponse

SecuritySnapshot.description: One evidence-only security projection for an unresolved incident revision.
SecuritySnapshot.title: SecuritySnapshot

SecurityTimelineEvent.description: One security-axis episode referenced by the exact incident assessment.
SecurityTimelineEvent.title: SecurityTimelineEvent

SnapshotInvalidation.description: One typed signal that one or more REST snapshots are stale.
SnapshotInvalidation.title: SnapshotInvalidation

SnapshotResource.description: Authoritative snapshots an invalidation may ask the browser to refetch.
SnapshotResource.title: SnapshotResource

StreamEventKind.description: Named SSE events understood by the product surface.
StreamEventKind.title: StreamEventKind

SuppressionKind.description:
Why an operator asked the platform to hold back.

``CHANGE_FREEZE`` forbids autonomous action without quieting anything: the
problem is still reported, we simply do not touch production during the
freeze. ``MAINTENANCE`` is the stronger claim that expected disruption on
named services is not worth reporting.
SuppressionKind.title: SuppressionKind

Symptom.description: One scored, human-legible piece of evidence about abnormal behavior.
Symptom.title: Symptom

SymptomEpisode.description:
A hysteresis-guarded lifecycle over repeated symptoms of one key.

An episode groups the recurring symptoms of a single ``(kind, service,
signal)`` into one durable incident-precursor. It opens only after a symptom
persists (breach persistence + a score deadband) and closes only after it
clears for long enough, so a momentary blip can never open one and a key can
never flap. Raw ``Symptom`` evidence is untouched; an episode only points at
it via the opening, peak and latest symptom ids.
SymptomEpisode.title: SymptomEpisode

SymptomKind.description: Deterministic evidence categories understood by the decision plane.
SymptomKind.title: SymptomKind

Verdict.description:
The fused, evidence-backed answer, with its differential diagnosis.

``verdict_class`` comes from the ordered rule table - crisp, operator-owned
and explainable. ``distribution`` is the same signatures read softly, so the
runner-up is visible rather than hidden. Every class that lost is recorded
in ``rejected_alternatives`` with the requirement it failed, so the answer
can be argued with rather than merely believed.
Verdict.title: Verdict

VerdictClass.description: What the fused evidence says is actually happening.
VerdictClass.title: VerdictClass

VerdictProbability.description: One member of the complete deterministic verdict distribution.
VerdictProbability.title: VerdictProbability

Verification.description:
The four deterministic checks a hypothesis must survive before it is acted on.

Nothing here proposes anything. Each check is arithmetic over telemetry and
committed topology, and all four must hold: a hypothesis that is merely
plausible is left unconfirmed, which downstream means pending review rather
than action.

``BOOTSTRAP`` is a vacuous pass, recorded as such and never as a
confirmation. It exists only so that an empty incident memory cannot make
confirmation impossible forever.
Verification.title: Verification

VerificationCheck.description: One non-LLM check and the evidence-derived reason for its answer.
VerificationCheck.title: VerificationCheck
